keypoints.name: Breadboards
keypoints.description: Breadboards are introduced as a solderless prototyping tool, good for early-stage design.  Both solderable and non-solderable types are described, along with compatible zip wire.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Breadboards are discussed at the beginning and mentioned throughout as the starting point for prototyping, but not the main focus.
representative_quotes: One of the easiest ways to start is with a breadboard.
Breadboards aren't really for final design, they're for the prototyping stage

keypoints.name: Padboards and Stripboards
keypoints.description: Padboards and stripboards are presented as more permanent alternatives to breadboards once a design is finalized. The video covers soldering techniques for padboards, how stripboards use connected rows for shared connections, and discusses their interchangeability.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: A dedicated video close-up shows the differences between them, and advantages of each are explained.
representative_quotes: Once you get past the breadboard stage, if you want it to be a little more permanent, you could use either a stripboard or a padboard.
Padboard is a general purpose circuit board with a through-hole design and one pad per hole.

keypoints.name: Standoffs
keypoints.description: Standoffs are presented as a solution to prevent shorts when using enclosures. They raise the board off the box bottom.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Standoffs are explained, and a use case for them is provided.
representative_quotes: they basically go right inside here and it keeps your board off of the box
